hooks.text: A city-killer asteroid hid in plain sight until just before impact.
Why did a massive asteroid vanish right in front of Earth's telescopes?
A space rock thirty times more powerful than Hiroshima almost hit us.

title: The Asteroid That Hid in Plain Sight
description: In 2019, a massive asteroid nearly struck Earth after dodging detection by appearing perfectly still in the night sky.

beats.text: A city-killer asteroid hid in plain sight until just before impact.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of a large asteroid in close proximity to Earth

beats.text: In July 2019, 2019 OK screamed past us at nearly 55,000 miles per hour.
beats.visual: Inner solar system orbit diagram showing the paths of Venus and Mars

beats.text: The football-field-sized rock missed our planet by about 45,000 miles.
beats.visual: Diagram showing the orbit of asteroid 2019 OK passing Earth

beats.text: That is less than one-fifth of the distance to the Moon.
beats.visual: Comparison graphic of the distance between Earth and the Moon

beats.text: An impact would have released over thirty times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Little Boy atomic bomb replica

beats.text: Survey telescopes like Pan-STARRS had actually photographed it earlier, but it went unrecognized.
beats.visual: Pan-STARRS telescope dome on Haleakala, Hawaii at night

beats.text: Because the asteroid was heading directly toward us, it appeared completely stationary.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of an asteroid heading directly toward the viewer

beats.text: Amateur astronomers Jacques, Pimentel, and Ribeiro finally spotted the threat before its approach.
beats.visual: Astronomical observatory dome under the southern night sky

beats.text: This Apollo-class rock won't return for 200 years, but it proved how a city-killer asteroid hid in plain sight.
beats.visual: Diagram showing the highly elliptical orbit of an Apollo-class asteroid

better_than_last: Delayed the resolution of the asteroid threat until the final beats to improve mid-script retention as per lessons from ep035.
